sample_unit: LDCT images (screens with presumed nonmalignant nodules)

links.outcome: AUC for predicting 1-year lung cancer risk, deep learning vs statistical model vs Lung-RADS on same data
links.effect: Recalibrated LCP-CNN AUC 0.87 vs LCRAT + CT 0.79 and Lung-RADS 0.69 (P < .001); lower 1-year delay risk at 66% biennial assignment (0.28% vs 0.60% vs 0.97%).
links.quote: The recalibrated LCP-CNN had substantially higher area under the curve (0.87) than LCRAT + CT (0.79) or Lung-RADS (0.69) to predict 1-year lung cancer risk (P < .001).

unlisted_practices: Recalibrating an imaging deep learning model to predict 1-year cancer detection to assign longer screening intervals to low-risk people

screen.reason: Evaluates the recalibration of an existing commercially developed deep learning model (LCP-CNN) to tailor lung cancer screening intervals (annual vs biennial) using retrospective clinical trial data.

primary.practice: model recalibration for risk-stratified screening intervals
